o: En efeto, fueron tantas las voces que don Quijote dio, que, abriendo de presto las puertas de la venta, salió el ventero, despavorido, a ver quién tales gritos daba, y los que estaban fuera hicieron lo mesmo.
t: In fact, the voices Don Quixote raised were so many that, hastily opening the doors of the inn, the innkeeper came out terrified to see who was making such cries, and those who were outside did the same.

o: Maritornes, que ya había despertado a las mismas voces, imaginando lo que podía ser, se fue al pajar y desató, sin que nadie lo viese, el cabestro que a don Quijote sostenía, y él dio luego en el suelo, a vista del ventero y de los caminantes, que, llegándose a él, le preguntaron qué tenía, que tales voces daba.
t: Maritornes, who had already been awakened by the very same cries and imagining what it might be, went to the hayloft and, unseen by anyone, untied the halter that Don Quixote was holding, and he immediately fell to the ground in full view of the innkeeper and the travelers, who, coming up to him, asked what was wrong with him, that he was making such cries.

o: Él, sin responder palabra, se quitó el cordel de la muñeca, y, levantándose en pie, subió sobre Rocinante, embrazó su adarga, enristró su lanzón, y, tomando buena parte del campo, volvió a medio galope, diciendo.
t: He, without saying a word, took the cord from his wrist and, rising to his feet, climbed onto Rocinante, tucked his shield under his arm, set his lance in the rest, and, taking a good stretch of the field, returned at a half gallop, saying:

o: — Cualquiera que dijere que yo he sido con justo título encantado, como mi señora la princesa Micomicona me dé licencia para ello, yo le desmiento, le rieto y desafío a singular batalla.
t: "Anyone who says that I have been justly enchanted, if my lady the princess Micomicona gives me leave to say so, I will give him the lie, refute him, and challenge him to single combat."

o: Admirados se quedaron los nuevos caminantes de las palabras de don Quijote, pero el ventero les quitó de aquella admiración, diciéndoles que era don Quijote, y que no había que hacer caso dél, porque estaba fuera de juicio.
t: The new travelers were astonished at Don Quixote's words, but the innkeeper dispelled their astonishment by telling them that this was Don Quixote, and that no heed was to be paid to him, because he was out of his senses.

o: Preguntáronle al ventero si acaso había llegado a aquella venta un muchacho de hasta edad de quince años, que venía vestido como mozo de mulas, de tales y tales señas, dando las mesmas que traía el amante de doña Clara.
t: They asked the innkeeper whether by any chance a lad of about fifteen years had come to that inn, dressed as a muleteer, with such and such marks, giving the same description as the one they had brought of Doña Clara's lover.

o: El ventero respondió que había tanta gente en la venta, que no había echado de ver en el que preguntaban.
t: The innkeeper replied that there was such a crowd in the inn that he had not noticed the one they were asking about.

o: Pero, habiendo visto uno dellos el coche donde había venido el oidor, dijo.
t: But, having seen among them the coach in which the judge had come, he said:

o: — Aquí debe de estar sin duda, porque éste es el coche que él dicen que sigue; quédese uno de nosotros a la puerta y entren los demás a buscarle; y aun sería bien que uno de nosotros rodease toda la venta, porque no se fuese por las bardas de los corrales.
t: "He must be here without a doubt, because this is the coach they say he follows; let one of us stay at the door and let the rest go in to look for him; and it would be well, too, if one of us went around the whole inn, in case he slipped out through the fences of the yards."

o: — Así se hará —respondió uno dellos.
t: "So it shall be," replied one of them.

o: Y, entrándose los dos dentro, uno se quedó a la puerta y el otro se fue a rodear la venta; todo lo cual veía el ventero, y no sabía atinar para qué se hacían aquellas diligencias, puesto que bien creyó que buscaban aquel mozo cuyas señas le habían dado.
t: And the two of them going inside, one stayed at the door and the other went around the inn; all of which the innkeeper saw, and he could not make out what those proceedings were for, since he rightly believed they were looking for that lad whose description they had given him.

o: Ya a esta sazón aclaraba el día; y, así por esto como por el ruido que don Quijote había hecho, estaban todos despiertos y se levantaban, especialmente doña Clara y Dorotea, que la una con sobresalto de tener tan cerca a su amante, y la otra con el deseo de verle, habían podido dormir bien mal aquella noche.
t: By this time the day was breaking; and both for this reason and because of the noise Don Quixote had made, everyone was awake and getting up, especially Doña Clara and Dorotea, who, the one startled at having her lover so close by, and the other longing to see him, had both slept very badly that night.

o: El hombre le trabó del brazo y le dijo.
t: The man seized him by the arm and said to him.

o: — Por cierto, señor don Luis, que responde bien a quien vos sois el hábito que tenéis, y que dice bien la cama en que os hallo al regalo con que vuestra madre os crió.
t: — By the way, sir don Luis, who answers so well to the person you are, the habit you keep, and who rightly says of the bed in which I find you at ease, with which your mother raised you.

o: Limpióse el mozo los soñolientos ojos y miró de espacio al que le tenía asido, y luego conoció que era criado de su padre, de que recibió tal sobresalto, que no acertó o no pudo hablarle palabra por un buen espacio.
t: The youth wiped his sleepy eyes and looked at the man who held him fast, and then he recognized him as a servant of his father, at which he was so startled that for a good while he could neither find the words nor speak them to him.

o: Y el criado prosiguió diciendo.
t: And the servant went on saying.

o: — Aquí no hay que hacer otra cosa, señor don Luis, sino prestar paciencia y dar la vuelta a casa, si ya vuestra merced no gusta que su padre y mi señor la dé al otro mundo, porque no se puede esperar otra cosa de la pena con que queda por vuestra ausencia.
t: — Here there is nothing to do, sir don Luis, but be patient and turn back toward home, if your grace does not care for your father and my lord to send him to the next world, because nothing else can be expected from the grief with which he is left because of your absence.

o: — Pues, ¿cómo supo mi padre —dijo don Luis— que yo venía este camino y en este traje?
t: — Then how did my father —said don Luis— know that I was coming this way and in this attire?

o: — Eso será como yo quisiere, o como el cielo lo ordenare —respondió don Luis.
t: — That will be as I wish, or as heaven shall order —answered don Luis.

o: — ¿Qué habéis de querer, o qué ha de ordenar el cielo, fuera de consentir en volveros?; porque no ha de ser posible otra cosa.
t: — What should I wish, or what should heaven order, other than consenting to your return; for nothing else can be possible.

o: Y con esto, y con lo que dél sabían de la buena voz que el cielo le había dado, vinieron todos en gran deseo de saber más particularmente quién era, y aun de ayudarle si alguna fuerza le quisiesen hacer; y así, se fueron hacia la parte donde aún estaba hablando y porfiando con su criado.
t: And with this, and with what they knew of him from the good reputation heaven had given him, they all came to a great desire to know more particularly who he was, and even to help him if any force should be used against him; and so they went toward the place where he was still talking and arguing with his servant.

o: Cardenio dijo a Dorotea que se volviesen al aposento, que él procuraría poner remedio en todo, y ellas lo hicieron.
t: Cardenio told Dorotea to go back to the room, that he would try to remedy everything, and they did so.

o: Ya estaban todos los cuatro que venían a buscar a don Luis dentro de la venta y rodeados dél, persuadiéndole que luego, sin detenerse un punto, volviese a consolar a su padre.
t: The four who had come to look for don Luis were already inside the inn and gathered around him, persuading him to return at once, without stopping a moment, to comfort his father.

o: Él respondió que en ninguna manera lo podía hacer hasta dar fin a un negocio en que le iba la vida, la honra y el alma.
t: He replied that in no way could he do so until he brought to a close a business in which his life, his honor, and his soul were at stake.

o: Apretáronle entonces los criados, diciéndole que en ningún modo volverían sin él, y que le llevarían, quisiese o no quisiese.
t: Then the servants pressed him, telling him that in no case would they go back without him, and that they would take him whether he wished it or not.

o: — Eso no haréis vosotros —replicó don Luis—, si no es llevándome muerto; aunque, de cualquiera manera que me llevéis, será llevarme sin vida.
t: — You shall not do that —replied don Luis—, unless by carrying me off dead; though, in whatever way you take me, it will be taking me away without life.

o: Ya a esta sazón habían acudido a la porfía todos los más que en la venta estaban, especialmente Cardenio, don Fernando, sus camaradas, el oidor, el cura, el barbero y don Quijote, que ya le pareció que no había necesidad de guardar más el castillo.
t: By this time all the others who were in the inn had come to the dispute, especially Cardenio, don Fernando, his companions, the oidor, the priest, the barber, and don Quixote, who now thought there was no need to guard the castle any longer.

o: Cardenio, como ya sabía la historia del mozo, preguntó a los que llevarle querían que qué les movía a querer llevar contra su voluntad aquel muchacho.
t: Cardenio, who already knew the story of the youth, asked those who wanted to take him what moved them to want to carry off against his will that young man.

o: — Muévenos —respondió uno de los cuatro— dar la vida a su padre, que por la ausencia deste caballero queda a peligro de perderla.
t: — What moves us —answered one of the four— is giving life to his father, who, because of this gentleman's absence, is in danger of losing it.

o: A esto dijo don Luis.
t: To this don Luis said.

o: — No hay para qué se dé cuenta aquí de mis cosas: yo soy libre, y volveré si me diere gusto, y si no, ninguno de vosotros me ha de hacer fuerza.
t: — There is no need to give account here of my affairs: I am free, and I will return if it please me, and if not, none of you shall force me.

o: — Harásela a vuestra merced la razón —respondió el hombre—; y, cuando ella.
t: — Your grace will be obeyed —answered the man—; and, when it is.

o: no bastare con vuestra merced, bastará con nosotros para hacer a lo que venimos y lo que somos obligados.
t: not enough with your grace, it will be enough with us to do what we have come for and what we are obliged to do.

o: — Sepamos qué es esto de raíz —dijo a este tiempo el oidor.
t: "Let us find out from the root what this is," said the judge at that moment.

o: Pero el hombre, que lo conoció, como vecino de su casa, respondió.
t: But the man, who knew him as a neighbor of his house, replied.

o: — ¿No conoce vuestra merced, señor oidor, a este caballero, que es el hijo de su vecino, el cual se ha ausentado de casa de su padre en el hábito tan indecente a su calidad como vuestra merced puede ver?
t: "Does your grace, sir judge, not know this gentleman, who is the son of your neighbor, who has left his father's house in a garb so unbecoming to his rank as your grace can see?"

o: Miróle entonces el oidor más atentamente y conocióle; y, abrazándole, dijo.
t: Then the judge looked at him more attentively and recognized him; and, embracing him, he said.

o: — ¿Qué niñerías son éstas, señor don Luis, o qué causas tan poderosas, que os hayan movido a venir desta manera, y en este traje, que dice tan mal con la calidad vuestra?
t: "What childish notions are these, sir Don Luis, or what reasons so powerful, that they have moved you to come in this manner, and in this attire, which so ill becomes your rank?"

o: Al mozo se le vinieron las lágrimas a los ojos, y no pudo responder palabra.
t: Tears came to the young man's eyes, and he could not answer a word.

o: El oidor dijo a los cuatro que se sosegasen, que todo se haría bien; y, tomando por la mano a don Luis, le apartó a una parte y le preguntó qué venida había sido aquélla.
t: The judge told the four of them to calm down, that everything would turn out well; and, taking Don Luis by the hand, he drew him aside and asked him what that visit had been.

o: La ventera y su hija no vieron a otro más desocupado para poder socorrerle que a don Quijote, a quien la hija de la ventera dijo.
t: The innkeeper's wife and her daughter saw no one more free to help him than Don Quixote, and the innkeeper's daughter said to him.

o: — Socorra vuestra merced, señor caballero, por la virtud que Dios le dio, a mi pobre padre, que dos malos hombres le están moliendo como a cibera.
t: "Help your grace, sir knight, by the virtue God gave you, my poor father, for two wicked men are beating him like a sieve."

o: A lo cual respondió don Quijote, muy de espacio y con mucha flema.
t: To which Don Quixote replied, very deliberately and with great composure.

o: — Fermosa doncella, no ha lugar por ahora vuestra petición, porque estoy impedido de entremeterme en otra aventura en tanto que no diere cima a una en que mi palabra me ha puesto.
t: "Fair damsel, there is no place for your petition at present, because I am barred from taking on another adventure until I have brought to a close one in which my word has placed me."

o: Mas lo que yo podré hacer por serviros es lo que ahora diré: corred y decid a vuestro padre que se entretenga en esa batalla lo mejor que pudiere, y que no se deje vencer en ningún modo, en tanto que yo pido licencia a la princesa Micomicona para poder socorrerle en su cuita; que si ella me la da, tened por cierto que yo le sacaré della.
t: But what I can do to serve you is what I shall now say: run and tell your father that he should hold out in that battle as best he can, and that he let himself be beaten in no way whatsoever, while I ask the princess Micomicona for leave to come to his aid in his distress; and if she grants it to me, take it as certain that I shall pull him out of there.

o: — ¡Pecadora de mí!
t: "Wretch that I am!"

o: —dijo a esto Maritornes, que estaba delante—: primero que vuestra merced alcance esa licencia que dice, estará ya mi señor en el otro mundo.
t: "said Maritornes, who was standing there—before your grace has obtained that leave you speak of, my master will already be in the other world."

o: — Dadme vos, señora, que yo alcance la licencia que digo —respondió don Quijote—; que, como yo la tenga, poco hará al caso que él esté en el otro mundo; que de allí le sacaré a pesar del mismo mundo que lo contradiga; o, por lo menos, os daré tal venganza de los que allá le hubieren enviado, que quedéis más que medianamente satisfechas.
t: "Give me leave, madam, to obtain the leave I speak of," replied Don Quixote; "for once I have it, it will matter little if he is in the other world; I shall pull him out of there in spite of the very world that contradicts me; or, at the very least, I shall give you such vengeance on those who sent him there that you will be more than moderately satisfied."

o: Y sin decir más se fue a poner de hinojos ante Dorotea, pidiéndole con palabras caballerescas y andantescas que la su grandeza fuese servida de darle licencia de acorrer y socorrer al castellano de aquel castillo, que estaba puesto en una grave mengua.
t: And without saying more, he went and knelt before Dorotea, begging her with chivalrous and knight-errant words that her highness would be pleased to grant him leave to go to the aid and succor of the Castilian in that castle, who was in a grave predicament.

o: La princesa se la dio de buen talante, y él luego, embrazando su adarga y poniendo mano a su espada, acudió a la puerta de la venta, adonde aún todavía traían los dos huéspedes a mal traer al ventero; pero, así como llegó, embazó y se estuvo quedo, aunque Maritornes y la ventera le decían que en qué se detenía, que socorriese a su señor y marido.
t: The princess granted it graciously, and he immediately, bracing his buckler and laying hand to his sword, hastened to the door of the inn, where the two guests were still giving the innkeeper a hard time; but as soon as he arrived he became embarrassed and stood still, though Maritornes and the innkeeper's wife kept asking him why he delayed, why he did not go to help their master and husband.

o: — Deténgome —dijo don Quijote— porque no me es lícito poner mano a la espada contra gente escuderil; pero llamadme aquí a mi escudero Sancho, que a él toca y atañe esta defensa y venganza.
t: "I am stopping," said Don Quixote, "because it is not lawful for me to draw the sword against men of the shield; but call me here my squire Sancho, for it is his task and concern to carry out this defense and vengeance."

o: Esto pasaba en la puerta de la venta, y en ella andaban las puñadas y mojicones muy en su punto, todo en daño del ventero y en rabia de Maritornes, la ventera y su hija, que se desesperaban de ver la cobardía de don Quijote, y de lo mal que lo pasaba su marido, señor y padre.
t: This was happening at the door of the inn, where the cuffing and rough handling were at their height, all to the harm of the innkeeper and to the fury of Maritornes, the innkeeper's wife and her daughter, who grew desperate at seeing Don Quixote's cowardice and how badly their husband, master and father was faring.

o: Pero dejémosle aquí, que no faltará quien le socorra, o si no, sufra y calle el que se atreve a más de a lo que sus fuerzas le prometen, y volvámonos atrás cincuenta pasos, a ver qué fue lo que don Luis respondió al oidor, que le dejamos aparte, preguntándole la causa de su venida a pie y de tan vil traje vestido.
t: But let us leave him here, for there will be no lack of someone to help him; and if not, let whoever ventures beyond what his strength promises suffer and keep quiet. And let us go back fifty paces to see what Don Luis answered the oidor, whom we set aside, asking him the reason for his coming on foot and in such a vile garb.

o: A lo cual el mozo, asiéndole fuertemente de las manos, como en señal de que algún gran dolor le apretaba el corazón, y derramando lágrimas en grande abundancia, le dijo.
t: To which the youth, gripping him firmly by the hands, as a sign that some great pain was squeezing his heart, and shedding tears in great abundance, said:

o: — Señor mío, yo no sé deciros otra cosa sino que desde el punto que quiso el cielo y facilitó nuestra vecindad que yo viese a mi señora doña Clara, hija vuestra y señora mía, desde aquel instante la hice dueño de mi voluntad; y si la vuestra, verdadero señor y padre mío, no lo impide, en este mesmo día ha de ser mi esposa.
t: "My lord, I can tell you nothing else than this: from the moment Heaven willed and made our neighborhood easy so that I might see my lady Doña Clara, your daughter and my lady, I made her mistress of my will; and if yours, true lord and father mine, does not prevent it, on this very day she shall be my wife."

o: Por ella dejé la casa de mi padre, y por ella me puse en este traje, para seguirla dondequiera que fuese, como la saeta al blanco, o como el marinero al norte.
t: For her I left my father's house, and for her I put on this garb, to follow her wherever she might go, like the arrow to the target, or like the sailor to the north.

o: Ella no sabe de mis deseos más de lo que ha podido entender de algunas veces que desde lejos ha visto llorar mis ojos.
t: She knows nothing of my desires beyond what she could gather from some of the times she has seen, from afar, my eyes weeping.

o: — ¡Ah don ladrón, que aquí os tengo!
t: "Ah, you thief! Here I have you!"

o: ¡Venga mi bacía y mi albarda, con todos mis aparejos que me robastes!
t: "Bring me my basin and my pack saddle, with all my gear that you stole from me!"

o: — ¡Aquí del rey y de la justicia, que, sobre cobrar mi hacienda, me quiere matar este ladrón salteador de caminos!
t: "Help, in the name of the king and of justice! For besides taking my property, this thief, this highwayman, means to kill me!"

o: — Mentís —respondió Sancho—, que yo no soy salteador de caminos; que en buena guerra ganó mi señor don Quijote estos despojos.
t: "You lie," answered Sancho, "for I am no highwayman; my master Don Quixote won these spoils in fair battle."

o: Ya estaba don Quijote delante, con mucho contento de ver cuán bien se defendía y ofendía su escudero, y túvole desde allí adelante por hombre de pro, y propuso en su corazón de armalle caballero en la primera ocasión que se le ofreciese, por parecerle que sería en él bien empleada la orden de la caballería.
t: Don Quixote was already in front, greatly pleased to see how well his squire defended himself and attacked, and from then on he held him for a man of worth, and resolved in his heart to knight him at the first opportunity that offered, since it seemed to him that the order of chivalry would be well bestowed on him.

o: Entre otras cosas que el barbero decía en el discurso de la pendencia, vino a decir.
t: Among other things the barber was saying in the course of the quarrel, he came to say:

o: — Señores, así esta albarda es mía como la muerte que debo a Dios, y así la conozco como si la hubiera parido; y ahí está mi asno en el establo, que no me dejará mentir; si no, pruébensela, y si no le viniere pintiparada, yo quedaré por infame.
t: "Gentlemen, this pack saddle is as much mine as the death I owe to God, and I know it as well as if I had given birth to it; and there is my ass in the stable, which will not let me lie; if not, try it on it, and if it does not fit me to a T, I shall stand for an infamous man."

o: Y hay más: que el mismo día que ella se me quitó, me quitaron también una bacía de azófar nueva, que no se había estrenado, que era señora de un escudo.
t: And more: on the very day she was taken from me, they also took from me a new brass basin, which had never been used, which was worth a escudo.

o: Aquí no se pudo contener don Quijote sin responder: y, poniéndose entre los dos y apartándoles, depositando la albarda en el suelo, que la tuviese de manifiesto hasta que la verdad se aclarase, dijo.
t: Don Quixote could not contain himself here without answering; and, placing himself between the two and setting them apart, and laying the pack saddle on the ground, so that it might be in plain view until the truth was cleared up, he said:

o: — ¡Porque vean vuestras mercedes clara y manifiestamente el error en que está este buen escudero, pues llama bacía a lo que fue, es y será yelmo de Mambrino, el cual se lo quité yo en buena guerra, y me hice señor dél con ligítima y lícita posesión!
t: "Let your worships see clearly and manifestly the error in which this good squire is, since he calls a basin what was, is, and shall be Mambrino's helmet, which I took from him in fair battle and made myself its rightful and lawful possessor!"

o: — ¡Pardiez, señor —dijo Sancho—, si no tenemos otra prueba de nuestra intención que la que vuestra merced dice, tan bacía es el yelmo de Malino como el jaez deste buen hombre albarda!
t: "God forgive you, sir," said Sancho, "if we have no other proof of our intent than what your worship says, then Mambrino's helmet is as much a basin as this good man's pack saddle is a saddle!"

o: — Haz lo que te mando —replicó don Quijote—, que no todas las cosas deste castillo han de ser guiadas por encantamento.
t: "Do as I command you," replied Don Quixote, "for not everything in this castle is to be guided by enchantment."

o: Sancho fue a do estaba la bacía y la trujo; y, así como don Quijote la vio, la tomó en las manos y dijo.
t: Sancho went where the basin was and brought it; and as soon as Don Quixote saw it, he took it in his hands and said:

o: — Miren vuestras mercedes con qué cara podía decir este escudero que ésta es bacía, y no el yelmo que yo he dicho; y juro por la orden de caballería que profeso que este yelmo fue el mismo que yo le quité, sin haber añadido en él ni quitado cosa alguna.
t: "See, your worships, with what face this squire could say that this is a basin and not the helmet I have spoken of; and I swear by the order of chivalry I profess that this helmet is the very one I took from him, without having added to it or taken from it anything at all."

o: — En eso no hay duda —dijo a esta sazón Sancho—, porque desde que mi señor le ganó hasta agora no ha hecho con él más de una batalla, cuando libró a los sin ventura encadenados; y si no fuera por este baciyelmo, no lo pasara entonces muy bien, porque hubo asaz de pedradas en aquel trance.
t: "There is no doubt about that," said Sancho at that moment, "for since my master won it until now he has done no more than one battle with it, when he freed the unfortunate men in chains; and if it had not been for this basin-helmet, he would not have come off so well then, for there was a good deal of stone-throwing in that business."

o: Donde se acaba de averiguar la duda del yelmo de Mambrino y de la albarda, y otras aventuras sucedidas, con toda verdad.
t: Where the doubt about Mambrino's helmet and the pack saddle, and other adventures that have occurred, has just been settled, in all truth.

o: — ¿Qué les parece a vuestras mercedes, señores —dijo el barbero—, de lo que afirman estos gentiles hombres, pues aún porfían que ésta no es bacía, sino yelmo?
t: "What do your worships think, gentlemen," said the barber, "of what these worthy men assert, since they still insist that this is not a barber's basin but a helmet?"

o: — Y quien lo contrario dijere —dijo don Quijote—, le haré yo conocer que miente, si fuere caballero, y si escudero, que remiente mil veces.
t: "And whoever says otherwise," said Don Quixote, "I will make him see that he lies—if he is a knight, and if he is a squire, that he lies a thousand times over."

o: Nuestro barbero, que a todo estaba presente, como tenía tan bien conocido el humor de don Quijote, quiso esforzar su desatino y llevar adelante la burla para que todos riesen, y dijo, hablando con el otro barbero.
t: Our barber, who had been present at everything, and who knew Don Quixote's humor so well, wanted to press his blunder and carry the joke forward so that everyone would laugh, and said, addressing the other barber.

o: — No, por cierto —dijo don Quijote—, porque le falta la mitad, que es la babera.
t: "No, certainly not," said Don Quixote, "because it is missing half of it, which is the visor."

o: — Así es —dijo el cura, que ya había entendido la intención de su amigo el barbero.
t: "That is true," said the priest, who had already grasped the intention of his friend the barber.

o: Y lo mismo confirmó Cardenio, don Fernando y sus camaradas; y aun el oidor, si no estuviera tan pensativo con el negocio de don Luis, ayudara, por su parte, a la burla; pero las veras de lo que pensaba le tenían tan suspenso, que poco o nada atendía a aquellos donaires.
t: Cardenio, Don Fernando and his companions confirmed the same; and even the oidor, if he had not been so absorbed in the affair of Don Luis, would have helped with his part in the jest; but the truth of what he was thinking held him so suspended that he paid little or no attention to those jests.

o: —dijo a esta sazón el barbero burlado—; ¿que es posible que tanta gente honrada diga que ésta no es bacía, sino yelmo?
t: "—said the duped barber at that moment—; is it possible that so many worthy people should say that this is not a basin but a helmet?"

o: Cosa parece ésta que puede poner en admiración a toda una Universidad, por discreta que sea.
t: This is a thing that might put a whole university, however discreet, in wonder.

o: Basta: si es que esta bacía es yelmo, también debe de ser esta albarda jaez de caballo, como este señor ha dicho.
t: Enough: if this basin is a helmet, then this pack saddle must also be a horse harness, as this gentleman has said.

o: — A mí albarda me parece —dijo don Quijote—, pero ya he dicho que en eso no me entremeto.
t: "To me it looks like a pack saddle," said Don Quixote, "but I have already said that I do not meddle in that."

o: — De que sea albarda o jaez —dijo el cura— no está en más de decirlo el señor don Quijote; que en estas cosas de la caballería todos estos señores y yo le damos la ventaja.
t: "Whether it is a pack saddle or a harness," said the priest, "is nothing more than a matter of saying, as far as the gentleman Don Quixote is concerned; in these matters of chivalry all these gentlemen and I give him the advantage."

o: — Por Dios, señores míos —dijo don Quijote—, que son tantas y tan estrañas las cosas que en este castillo, en dos veces que en él he alojado, me han sucedido, que no me atreva a decir afirmativamente ninguna cosa de lo que acerca de lo que en él se contiene se preguntare, porque imagino que cuanto en él se trata va por vía de encantamento.
t: "By God, my lords," said Don Quixote, "the things that have happened to me in this castle, in the two times I have lodged here, are so many and so strange that I dare not affirm anything about what it contains, should anyone ask me about it; for I imagine that everything dealt with here goes by way of enchantment."

o: La primera vez me fatigó mucho un moro encantado que en él hay, y a Sancho no le fue muy bien con otros sus secuaces; y anoche estuve colgado deste brazo casi dos horas, sin saber cómo ni cómo no vine a caer en aquella desgracia.
t: The first time, an enchanted Moor who is in it wearied me greatly, and Sancho fared no too well with some other followers of his; and last night I hung by this arm for nearly two hours, without knowing how or how I came to fall into that misfortune.

o: Así que, ponerme yo agora en cosa de tanta confusión a dar mi parecer, será caer en juicio temerario.
t: So, for me now to venture into a matter of such confusion and give my opinion would be to fall into a rash judgment.

o: En lo que toca a lo que dicen que ésta es bacía, y no yelmo, ya yo tengo respondido; pero, en lo de declarar si ésa es albarda o jaez, no me atrevo a dar sentencia difinitiva: sólo lo dejo al buen parecer de vuestras mercedes.
t: As for what they say, that this is a basin and not a helmet, I have already given my answer; but as to declaring whether that one is a pack saddle or a harness, I do not dare pronounce a final sentence: I leave it to the good judgment of your worships.

o: Quizá por no ser armados caballeros, como yo lo soy, no tendrán que ver con vuestras mercedes los encantamentos deste lugar, y tendrán los entendimientos libres, y podrán juzgar de las cosas deste castillo como ellas son real y verdaderamente, y no como a mí me parecían.
t: Perhaps, for not being armed knights as I am, your worships will have nothing to do with the enchantments of this place, and will have their wits free, and be able to judge the things of this castle as they truly and really are, and not as they seemed to me.

o: — No hay duda —respondió a esto don Fernando—, sino que el señor don Quijote ha dicho muy bien hoy que a nosotros toca la difinición deste caso; y, porque vaya con más fundamento, yo tomaré en secreto los votos destos señores, y de lo que resultare daré entera y clara noticia.
t: "There is no doubt," Don Fernando replied, "but that the gentleman Don Quixote has said very well today that it is up to us to settle this case; and, so that it be done with more solid ground, I will take the votes of these gentlemen in secret, and I will give full and clear account of the outcome."

o: Y, después que hubo tomado los votos de aquellos que a don Quijote conocían, dijo en alta voz.
t: And, after he had taken the votes of those who knew Don Quixote, he said aloud.

o: — No la tenga yo en el cielo —dijo el sobrebarbero— si todos vuestras mercedes no se engañan, y que así parezca mi ánima ante Dios como ella me parece a mí albarda, y no jaez; pero allá van leyes..., etcétera; y no digo más; y en verdad que no estoy borracho: que no me he desayunado, si de pecar no.
t: "May I not go to heaven," said the master barber, "if all your worships are not mistaken, and if it does not appear to my soul before God as it appears to me that this is a pack saddle and not a harness; but laws go their own way... and so on; and I say no more; and truly I am not drunk: I have not had my breakfast, if that is a sin."

o: No menos causaban risa las necedades que decía el barbero que los disparates de don Quijote, el cual a esta sazón dijo.
t: No less laughter did the barber's follies cause than the absurdities of Don Quixote, who at that moment said:

o: — Aquí no hay más que hacer, sino que cada uno tome lo que es suyo, y a quien Dios se la dio, San Pedro se la bendiga.
t: "There is nothing to be done here, but for each to take what is his own, and may God bless whoever it belongs to, as Saint Peter blesses it."

o: Uno de los cuatro dijo.
t: One of the four said.

o: —y arrojóle redondo—, que no me den a mí a entender cuantos hoy viven en el mundo al revés de que ésta no sea bacía de barbero y ésta albarda de asno.
t: "—and he flung it round—let no one make me understand how many people there are today in the world who are so backward that this is not a barber's basin and this is not a donkey's pack saddle."

o: — Bien podría ser de borrica —dijo el cura.
t: "It could well be a she-donkey's," said the priest.

o: — Tanto monta —dijo el criado—, que el caso no consiste en eso, sino en si es o no es albarda, como vuestras mercedes dicen.
t: "It makes no difference," said the squire, "for the point is not that, but whether it is or is not a pack saddle, as your graces say."

o: Oyendo esto uno de los cuadrilleros que habían entrado, que había oído la pendencia y quistión, lleno de cólera y de enfado, dijo.
t: Hearing this, one of the men-at-arms who had come in, who had overheard the dispute and argument, full of anger and fury, said:

o: — Tan albarda es como mi padre; y el que otra cosa ha dicho o dijere debe de estar hecho uva.
t: "It is as much a pack saddle as my father is; and whoever has said or shall say otherwise must be a raisin."

o: — Mentís como bellaco villano —respondió don Quijote.
t: "You lie, you villainous knave," replied Don Quixote.

o: Y, alzando el lanzón, que nunca le dejaba de las manos, le iba a descargar tal golpe sobre la cabeza, que, a no desviarse el cuadrillero, se le dejara allí tendido.
t: And, raising the lance, which never left his hands, he was about to deal him such a blow on the head that, had the man-at-arms not dodged, he would have left him stretched out there.

o: El lanzón se hizo pedazos en el suelo, y los demás cuadrilleros, que vieron tratar mal a su compañero, alzaron la voz pidiendo favor a la Santa Hermandad.
t: The lance was smashed to pieces on the ground, and the other men-at-arms, seeing their companion ill-treated, raised their voices, crying to the Holy Brotherhood for aid.

o: El ventero, que era de la cuadrilla, entró al punto por su varilla y por su espada, y se puso al lado de sus compañeros; los criados de don Luis rodearon a don Luis, porque con el alboroto no se les fuese; el barbero, viendo la casa revuelta, tornó a asir de su albarda, y lo mismo hizo Sancho; don Quijote puso mano a su espada y arremetió a los cuadrilleros.
t: The innkeeper, who belonged to the band, straightway entered with his staff and his sword and took his place beside his companions; Don Luis's servants surrounded Don Luis, so that amid the uproar he might not slip away; the barber, seeing the house in confusion, seized his pack saddle again, and Sancho did the same; Don Quixote laid hand on his sword and charged the men-at-arms.

o: Don Luis daba voces a sus criados que le dejasen a él y acorriesen a don Quijote, y a Cardenio, y a don Fernando, que todos favorecían a don Quijote.
t: Don Luis was shouting to his servants to let him go and help Don Quixote, and Cardenio, and Don Fernando, for all of them favored Don Quixote.

o: El cura daba voces, la ventera gritaba, su hija se afligía, Maritornes lloraba, Dorotea estaba confusa, Luscinda suspensa y doña Clara desmayada.
t: The priest was shouting, the innkeeper's wife was screaming, her daughter was distressed, Maritornes was weeping, Dorothea was confused, Luscinda was in suspense, and Doña Clara had fainted.

o: El barbero aporreaba a Sancho, Sancho molía al barbero; don Luis, a quien un criado suyo se atrevió a asirle del brazo porque no se fuese, le dio una puñada que le bañó los dientes en sangre; el oidor le defendía, don Fernando tenía debajo de sus pies a un cuadrillero, midiéndole el cuerpo con ellos muy a su sabor.
t: The barber was beating Sancho, Sancho was grinding the barber; Don Luis, whose servant had the audacity to seize him by the arm so that he might not go, gave him a punch that bathed his teeth in blood; the judge defended him, Don Fernando had one of the men-at-arms underfoot, measuring his body with his feet very much to his liking.

o: El ventero tornó a reforzar la voz, pidiendo favor a la Santa Hermandad: de modo que toda la venta era llantos, voces, gritos, confusiones, temores, sobresaltos, desgracias, cuchilladas, mojicones, palos, coces y efusión de sangre.
t: The innkeeper once more raised his voice, crying to the Holy Brotherhood for aid: so that the whole inn was tears, voices, shouts, confusion, fears, frights, mishaps, knife wounds, slaps, cudgels, kicks, and streams of blood.

o: Y, en la mitad deste caos, máquina y laberinto de cosas, se le representó en la memoria de don Quijote que se veía metido de hoz y de coz en la discordia del campo de Agramante; y así dijo, con voz que atronaba la venta.
t: And in the midst of this chaos, this machine and labyrinth of things, it came to Don Quixote's memory that he saw himself in the thick of the discord of the field of Agramante; and so he said, in a voice that thundered through the inn:

o: — ¡Ténganse todos; todos envainen; todos se sosieguen; óiganme todos, si todos quieren quedar con vida!
t: "Let all of you stop; let all of you draw your swords; let all of you calm down; listen to me, all of you, if you want to end up alive!"

o: A cuya gran voz, todos se pararon, y él prosiguió diciendo.
t: At this great cry, everyone stopped, and he went on saying:

o: — ¿No os dije yo, señores, que este castillo era encantado, y que alguna región de demonios debe de habitar en él?
t: "Did I not tell you, gentlemen, that this castle was enchanted, and that some region of demons must dwell in it?"

o: En confirmación de lo cual, quiero que veáis por vuestros ojos cómo se ha pasado aquí y trasladado entre nosotros la discordia del campo de Agramante.
t: In confirmation of which, I want you all to see with your own eyes how the discord of the field of Agramante has been transferred and passed on here among us.

o: Mirad cómo allí se pelea por la espada, aquí por el caballo, acullá por el águila, acá por el yelmo, y todos peleamos, y todos no nos entendemos.
t: See how there they fight for the sword, here for the horse, yonder for the eagle, here for the helmet, and we all fight, and all of us fail to understand one another.

o: Venga, pues, vuestra merced, señor oidor, y vuestra merced, señor cura, y el uno sirva de rey Agramante, y el otro de rey Sobrino, y pónganos en paz; porque por Dios Todopoderoso que es gran bellaquería que tanta gente principal como aquí estamos se mate por causas tan livianas.
t: Come now, your worship, sir judge, and your worship, sir curate, and let one play King Agramante and the other King Sobrino, and put us all at peace; for, by God Almighty, it would be a great piece of folly that so many notable people as are gathered here should kill each other over such trivial matters.

o: Sólo el ventero porfiaba que se habían de castigar las insolencias de aquel loco, que a cada paso le alborotaba la venta.
t: Only the innkeeper was insisting that the outrages of that madman, who stirred up the inn at every turn, must be punished.

o: Finalmente, el rumor se apaciguó por entonces, la albarda se quedó por jaez hasta el día del juicio, y la bacía por yelmo y la venta por castillo en la imaginación de don Quijote.
t: In short, the uproar was quieted for the time being, the pack-saddle remained as a harness until the day of judgment, and the basin for a helmet and the inn for a castle in the imagination of Don Quixote.

o: Puestos, pues, ya en sosiego, y hechos amigos todos a persuasión del oidor y del cura, volvieron los criados de don Luis a porfiarle que al momento se viniese con ellos; y, en tanto que él con ellos se avenía, el oidor comunicó con don Fernando, Cardenio y el cura qué debía hacer en aquel caso, contándoseles con las razones que don Luis le había dicho.
t: So, once they were at peace and all had become friends at the urging of the judge and the curate, Don Luis's servants began pressing him to come away with them at once; and while he was making terms with them, the judge communicated with Don Fernando, Cardenio, and the curate what was to be done in that case, telling them the reasons Don Luis had given him.

o: Entendida, pues, de los cuatro la calidad de don Fernando y la intención de don Luis, determinaron entre ellos que los tres se volviesen a contar lo que pasaba a su padre, y el otro se quedase a servir a don Luis, y a no dejalle hasta que ellos volviesen por él, o viese lo que su padre les ordenaba.
t: Having thus learned the character of Don Fernando and the intention of Don Luis, the four of them determined among themselves that the three should go back and tell their father what was happening, while the other would stay to serve Don Luis and not leave him until they returned for him, or until he saw what his father commanded them.

o: Y, apenas se hubo certificado, cuando, recogiendo su pergamino, en la izquierda tomó el mandamiento, y con la derecha asió a don Quijote del cuello fuertemente, que no le dejaba alentar, y a grandes voces decía.
t: And scarcely had this been settled when, gathering up his parchment, he took the writ in his left hand and with his right seized Don Quixote firmly by the neck, so that he could not get his breath, and he cried out in a loud voice:

o: — ¡Favor a la Santa Hermandad!
t: — Help, in the name of the Holy Brotherhood!

o: Y, para que se vea que lo pido de veras, léase este mandamiento, donde se contiene que se prenda a este salteador de caminos.
t: And so that you may see that I ask this in earnest, let this writ be read, in which it is contained that this highwayman is to be arrested.

o: El ventero, que por fuerza había de favorecer a los de su oficio, acudió luego a dalle favor.
t: The innkeeper, who was bound by force to favor those of his trade, came at once to give him aid.

o: La ventera, que vio de nuevo a su marido en pendencias, de nuevo alzó la voz, cuyo tenor le llevaron luego Maritornes y su hija, pidiendo favor al cielo y a los que allí estaban.
t: The innkeeper's wife, seeing her husband once more in trouble, raised her voice again, and Maritornes and her daughter soon carried the tenor of it, calling for help from heaven and from those who were there.

o: Sancho dijo, viendo lo que pasaba.
t: Sancho said, seeing what was happening.

o: — ¡Vive el Señor, que es verdad cuanto mi amo dice de los encantos deste castillo, pues no es posible vivir una hora con quietud en él!
t: — God alive, it's true everything my master says about the enchantments of this castle, for it's not possible to live a single hour in it with any peace!

o: Reíase de oír decir estas razones don Quijote; y, con mucho sosiego, dijo.
t: Don Quixote laughed to hear these words, and said, very calmly:

o: — Venid acá, gente soez y malnacida: ¿saltear de caminos llamáis al dar libertad a los encadenados, soltar los presos, acorrer a los miserables, alzar los caídos, remediar los menesterosos?
t: — Come here, you base and ill-born rabble: is it highway robbery, this, to give freedom to the chained, to loose the prisoners, to succor the wretched, to raise up the fallen, to relieve the needy?

o: ¡Ah gente infame, digna por vuestro bajo y vil entendimiento que el cielo no os comunique el valor que se encierra en la caballería andante, ni os dé a entender el pecado e ignorancia en que estáis en no reverenciar la sombra, cuanto más la asistencia, de cualquier caballero andante!
t: Oh, infamous lot, worthy by your low and vile understanding that heaven should not grant you the valor that is locked up in knight-errantry, nor make you understand the sin and ignorance in which you lie in not reverencing the shadow, let alone the presence, of any knight-errant!

o: Venid acá, ladrones en cuadrilla, que no cuadrilleros, salteadores de caminos con licencia de la Santa Hermandad; decidme: ¿quién fue el ignorante que firmó mandamiento de prisión contra un tal caballero como yo soy?
t: Come here, you thieves in a gang—not even a band of brigands, but highwaymen with a license from the Holy Brotherhood; tell me: who was the ignoramus who signed the writ of arrest against a knight such as I am?

o: ¿Quién el que ignoró que son esentos de todo judicial fuero los caballeros andantes, y que su ley es su espada; sus fueros, sus bríos; sus premáticas, su voluntad?
t: Who was he who did not know that knights-errant are exempt from all judicial authority, and that their law is their sword, their statutes their valor, their ordinances their will?

o: ¿Quién fue el mentecato, vuelvo a decir, que no sabe que no hay secutoria de hidalgo con tantas preeminencias, ni esenciones, como la que adquiere un caballero andante el día que se arma caballero y se entrega al duro ejercicio de la caballería?
t: Who was the fool, I say again, who does not know that there is no execution of a gentleman with so many prerogatives and exemptions as are acquired by a knight-errant on the day he is dubbed knight and devotes himself to the hard exercise of chivalry?

o: ¿Qué caballero andante pagó pecho, alcabala, chapín de la reina, moneda forera, portazgo ni barca?
t: What wandering knight ever paid tax, alcabala, the queen's chopine, the forced levy, the tollbridge or the ferry?

o: ¿Qué sastre le llevó hechura de vestido que le hiciese?
t: What tailor ever took his measure for a suit of clothes to fit him?

o: ¿Qué castellano le acogió en su castillo que le hiciese pagar el escote?
t: What Castilian ever took him into his castle and made him pay for his keep?

o: ¿Qué rey no le asentó a su mesa?
t: What king never seated him at his table?

o: ¿Qué doncella no se le aficionó y se le entregó rendida, a todo su talante y voluntad?
t: What maiden never fell in love with him and surrendered to him, wholly and completely, in body and will?

o: Y, finalmente, ¿qué caballero andante ha habido, hay ni habrá en el mundo, que no tenga bríos para dar él solo cuatrocientos palos a cuatrocientos cuadrilleros que se le pongan delante?
t: And, finally, what wandering knight has there ever been, is there, or will there be in the world, who lacks the spirit to give four hundred blows all by himself to four hundred squires who set themselves against him?

o: De la notable aventura de los cuadrilleros, y la gran ferocidad de nuestro buen caballero don Quijote.
t: Of the notable adventure of the squires, and the great ferocity of our good knight Don Quixote.

o: — Con todo eso —dijo el cura—, por esta vez no le habéis de llevar, ni aun él dejará llevarse, a lo que yo entiendo.
t: "All the same," said the curate, "this time you are not to take him, nor will he let himself be taken, as I see it."

o: En efeto, tanto les supo el cura decir, y tantas locuras supo don Quijote hacer, que más locos fueran que no él los cuadrilleros si no conocieran la falta de don Quijote; y así, tuvieron por bien de apaciguarse, y aun de ser medianeros de hacer las paces entre el barbero y Sancho Panza, que todavía asistían con gran rancor a su pendencia.
t: In effect, the curate knew so well how to speak, and Don Quixote knew so well how to act madly, that the squires would have been madder than he was had they not known Don Quixote's deficiency; and so they thought it well to calm down, and even to serve as mediators in making peace between the barber and Sancho Panza, who were still present, nursing a great grudge in their quarrel.

o: Zoraida, aunque no entendía bien todos los sucesos que había visto, se entristecía y alegraba a bulto, conforme veía y notaba los semblantes a cada uno, especialmente de su español, en quien tenía siempre puestos los ojos y traía colgada el alma.
t: Zoraida, though she did not fully understand all the events she had witnessed, grew sad and happy in bulk, as she saw and noticed the expressions of each of them, especially of her Spaniard, on whom she always kept her eyes fixed and held her soul suspended.

o: El ventero, a quien no se le pasó por alto la dádiva y recompensa que el cura había hecho al barbero, pidió el escote de don Quijote, con el menoscabo de sus cueros y falta de vino, jurando que no saldría de la venta Rocinante, ni el jumento de Sancho, sin que se le pagase primero hasta el último ardite.
t: The innkeeper, who had not let slip the gift and reward the curate had given the barber, demanded payment of Don Quixote's share, on account of the loss of his wineskins and the lack of wine, swearing that neither Rocinante nor Sancho's donkey would leave the inn until he had been paid down to the last farthing.

o: Así que, señora mía, prevengamos, como tengo dicho, con nuestra diligencia sus designios, y partámonos luego a la buena ventura; que no está más de tenerla vuestra grandeza como desea, de cuanto yo tarde de verme con vuestro contrario.
t: So, my lady, let us forestall, as I have said, her designs with our diligence, and let us set out forthwith upon good fortune; for it is no further from your greatness having it as you wish than my delay in seeing myself face to face with your adversary.

o: Calló y no dijo más don Quijote, y esperó con mucho sosiego la respuesta de la fermosa infanta; la cual, con ademán señoril y acomodado al estilo de don Quijote, le respondió desta manera.
t: Don Quixote fell silent and said no more, and waited with great composure for the reply of the beautiful princess; who, with a lordly air suited to Don Quixote's style, answered him in this manner.

o: — Yo os agradezco, señor caballero, el deseo que mostráis tener de favorecerme en mi gran cuita, bien así como caballero, a quien es anejo y concerniente favorecer los huérfanos y menesterosos; y quiera el cielo que el vuestro y mi deseo se cumplan, para que veáis que hay agradecidas mujeres en el mundo.
t: "I thank you, sir knight, for the desire you show to do me aid in my great distress, as befits a knight, to whom it is proper and incumbent to favour the orphaned and the needy; and may heaven grant that your wish and mine be fulfilled, so that you may see that there are grateful women in the world."

o: Y en lo de mi partida, sea luego; que yo no tengo más voluntad que la vuestra: disponed vos de mí a toda vuestra guisa y talante; que la que una vez os entregó la defensa de su persona y puso en vuestras manos la restauración de sus señoríos no ha de querer ir contra lo que la vuestra prudencia ordenare.
t: And as for my departure, let it be at once; for I have no will but yours: dispose of me as you please, entirely to your liking and pleasure; for she who once entrusted to you the defence of her person and placed in your hands the restoration of her dominions will not wish to go against what your prudence shall ordain.

o: — A la mano de Dios —dijo don Quijote—; pues así es que una señora se me humilla, no quiero yo perder la ocasión de levantalla y ponella en su heredado trono.
t: "God's will be done," said Don Quixote; "for since a lady humbles herself to me, I do not want to lose the chance to raise her and set her upon her ancestral throne."

o: La partida sea luego, porque me va poniendo espuelas al deseo y al camino lo que suele decirse que en la tardanza está el peligro.
t: Let the departure be at once, for what is commonly said to be in delay is danger is spurring me on in desire and in the road.

o: Y, pues no ha criado el cielo, ni visto el infierno, ninguno que me espante ni acobarde, ensilla, Sancho, a Rocinante, y apareja tu jumento y el palafrén de la reina, y despidámonos del castellano y destos señores, y vamos de aquí luego al punto.
t: And since there is none whom heaven has raised or hell seen who may frighten or daunt me, saddle Rocinante, Sancho, and get your donkey and the queen's palfrey ready, and let us take leave of the Castilian and these gentlemen, and let us go from here straight to the point.

o: Sancho, que a todo estaba presente, dijo, meneando la cabeza a una parte y a otra.
t: Sancho, who had been present throughout, said, shaking his head from side to side.

o: — ¡Ay señor, señor, y cómo hay más mal en el aldegüela que se suena, con perdón sea dicho de las tocadas honradas!
t: — Oh, sir, sir, and how much more evil there is in the village than is talked about, with pardon to the honest folk!

o: — ¿Qué mal puede haber en ninguna aldea, ni en todas las ciudades del mundo, que pueda sonarse en menoscabo mío, villano?
t: — What evil can there be in any village, or in all the cities of the world, that could be talked about to my discredit, you villain?

o: — Si vuestra merced se enoja —respondió Sancho—, yo callaré, y dejaré de decir lo que soy obligado como buen escudero, y como debe un buen criado decir a su señor.
t: — If your grace grows angry —answered Sancho— I will shut up and stop saying what I am obliged to say as a good squire, and as a good servant ought to say to his master.

o: — Di lo que quisieres —replicó don Quijote—, como tus palabras no se encaminen a ponerme miedo; que si tú le tienes, haces como quien eres, y si yo no le tengo, hago como quien soy.
t: — Say what you will —replied Don Quixote— as long as your words are not aimed at making me afraid; for if you are afraid, you act as what you are, and if I am not afraid, I act as what I am.

o: — No es eso, ¡pecador fui yo a Dios!
t: — That isn't it; I was a sinner before God!

o: —respondió Sancho—, sino que yo tengo por cierto y por averiguado que esta señora que se dice ser reina del gran reino Micomicón no lo es más que mi madre; porque, a ser lo que ella dice, no se anduviera hocicando con alguno de los que están en la rueda, a vuelta de cabeza y a cada traspuesta.
t: —answered Sancho— but I hold for certain and beyond doubt that this lady who claims to be queen of the great kingdom of Micomicón is no more than my mother; because, if she were what she says, she wouldn't be nosing about with one of the fellows in the wheel, turning her head round and about and at every turn.

o: ¡Oh, válame Dios, y cuán grande que fue el enojo que recibió don Quijote, oyendo las descompuestas palabras de su escudero!
t: Oh, may God help me, and how great was the anger that Don Quixote felt, hearing the uncouth words of his squire!

o: Digo que fue tanto, que, con voz atropellada y tartamuda lengua, lanzando vivo fuego por los ojos, dijo.
t: I say it was so great that, with a voice that tumbled over itself and a stammering tongue, his eyes spitting living fire, he said:

o: — ¡Oh bellaco villano, mal mirado, descompuesto, ignorante, infacundo, deslenguado, atrevido, murmurador y maldiciente!
t: — Oh, you rascally villain, ill-considered, uncouth, ignorant, foul-mouthed, loose-tongued, bold, muttering, and cursing!

o: ¿Tales palabras has osado decir en mi presencia y en la destas ínclitas señoras, y tales deshonestidades y atrevimientos osaste poner en tu confusa imaginación?
t: Have you dared to say such words in my presence and in that of these noble ladies, and have you dared to put such dishonorities and impudent claims into your muddled imagination?

o: ¡Vete de mi presencia, monstruo de naturaleza, depositario de mentiras, almario de embustes, silo de bellaquerías, inventor de maldades, publicador de sandeces, enemigo del decoro que se debe a las reales personas!
t: — Begone from my presence, monster of nature, storehouse of lies, sack of deceit, silo of trickery, inventor of villainies, publisher of follies, enemy of the respect owed to royal persons!

o: ¡Vete; no parezcas delante de mí, so pena de mi ira!
t: — Begone; do not appear before me, on pain of my wrath!

o: Y, diciendo esto, enarcó las cejas, hinchó los carrillos, miró a todas partes, y dio con el pie derecho una gran patada en el suelo, señales todas de la ira que encerraba en sus entrañas.
t: And saying this, he raised his eyebrows, puffed out his cheeks, looked all around, and gave a great kick with his right foot against the ground—all signs of the anger he held in his entrails.

o: A cuyas palabras y furibundos ademanes quedó Sancho tan encogido y medroso, que se holgara que en aquel instante se abriera debajo de sus pies la tierra y le tragara.
t: At whose words and furious gestures Sancho was so shrunk and terrified that he would have been glad if the earth had opened beneath his feet at that moment and swallowed him up.

o: Y no supo qué hacerse, sino volver las espaldas y quitarse de la enojada presencia de su señor.
t: And he did not know what to do, except turn his back and remove himself from his angry master's presence.

o: Pero la discreta Dorotea, que tan entendido tenía ya el humor de don Quijote, dijo, para templarle la ira.
t: But the discreet Dorothea, who already understood Don Quixote's humor so well, said, to temper his anger.

o: — Ansí es y ansí será —dijo don Fernando—; por lo cual debe vuestra merced, señor don Quijote, perdonalle y reducille al gremio de su gracia, sicut erat in principio, antes que las tales visiones le sacasen de juicio.
t: — So it is and so it shall be —said Don Fernando—; and so your grace, sir Don Quixote, must forgive him and bring him back into the fold of your grace, sicut erat in principio, before such visions drove him out of his mind.

o: Don Quijote respondió que él le perdonaba, y el cura fue por Sancho, el cual vino muy humilde, y, hincándose de rodillas, pidió la mano a su amo; y él se la dio, y, después de habérsela dejado besar, le echó la bendición, diciendo.
t: Don Quixote replied that he forgave him, and the priest went for Sancho, who came very humbly and, kneeling, asked his master's permission; and he granted it, and after letting him kiss his hand, he gave him his blessing, saying:

o: — Agora acabarás de conocer, Sancho hijo, ser verdad lo que yo otras muchas veces te he dicho de que todas las cosas deste castillo son hechas por vía de encantamento.
t: — Now you will finish learning, Sancho my son, that what I have told you many times before is true: that everything in this castle is made by way of enchantment.

o: — Así lo creo yo —dijo Sancho—, excepto aquello de la manta, que realmente sucedió por vía ordinaria.
t: — So I believe —said Sancho— except for the blanket, which really happened in the ordinary way.

o: — No lo creas —respondió don Quijote—; que si así fuera, yo te vengara entonces, y aun agora; pero ni entonces ni agora pude ni vi en quién tomar venganza de tu agravio.
t: "Don't believe it," replied Don Quixote, "for if it were so, I would avenge you then, and even now; but neither then nor now could I find anyone on whom to take vengeance for your wrong."

o: Hecho esto, con grandísimo silencio se entraron adonde él estaba durmiendo y descansando de las pasadas refriegas.
t: This done, with the utmost silence they entered where he was sleeping and resting after the past skirmishes.

o: Tomáronle luego en hombros, y, al salir del aposento, se oyó una voz temerosa, todo cuanto la supo formar el barbero, no el del albarda, sino el otro, que decía.
t: They then took him up on their shoulders, and as they came out of the room, a fearsome voice was heard, formed up by everything the barber could muster—not the barber of the pack-saddle, but the other one—which said:

o: Y esto será antes que el seguidor de la fugitiva ninfa faga dos vegadas la visita de las lucientes imágines con su rápido y natural curso.
t: And this shall come before the follower of the fleeing nymph twice visits the shining images with his swift and natural course.

o: Y asegúrote, de parte de la sabia Mentironiana, que tu salario te sea pagado, como lo verás por la obra; y sigue las pisadas del valeroso y encantado caballero, que conviene que vayas donde paréis entrambos.
t: And I assure you, on behalf of the wise Mentironian, that your wages shall be paid you, as you shall see by the deed; and follow the footsteps of the valorous and enchanted knight, for it is fitting that you go where you both halt.

o: Y, porque no me es lícito decir otra cosa, a Dios quedad, que yo me vuelvo adonde yo me sé.
t: And, since I am not permitted to say otherwise, farewell to God; for I return where I know myself to be.

o: Y, al acabar de la profecía, alzó la voz de punto, y diminuyóla después, con tan tierno acento, que aun los sabidores de la burla estuvieron por creer que era verdad lo que oían.
t: And when he had finished the prophecy, he raised his voice, and then lowered it again with such a tender accent that even those who knew the joke were on the point of believing what they heard was true.

o: Quedó don Quijote consolado con la escuchada profecía, porque luego coligió de todo en todo la significación de ella; y vio que le prometían el verse ayuntados en santo y debido matrimonio con su querida Dulcinea del Toboso, de cuyo felice vientre saldrían los cachorros, que eran sus hijos, para gloria perpetua de la Mancha.
t: Don Quixote was comforted by the prophecy he had heard, for he soon gathered from the whole of it its meaning; and he saw that they promised him the meeting and union in holy and due marriage with his beloved Dulcinea of Toboso, from whose happy womb would come the whelps, who were his children, to the perpetual glory of La Mancha.

o: Y, creyendo esto bien y firmemente, alzó la voz, y, dando un gran suspiro, dijo.
t: And, believing this well and firmly, he raised his voice and, giving a great sigh, said:

o: Sancho Panza se le inclinó con mucho comedimiento, y le besó entrambas las manos, porque la una no pudiera, por estar atadas entrambas.
t: Sancho Panza bowed to him with great courtesy, and kissed both his hands, for he could not kiss but one, since both were bound.

o: Luego tomaron la jaula en hombros aquellas visiones, y la acomodaron en el carro de los bueyes.
t: Then those visions took the cage on their shoulders and settled it on the cart drawn by the oxen.
